title: The neuropores close

objective.text: Order the last events that seal the neural tube.

body.general: What happens to the two open ends of the neural tube? These openings are the neuropores [f1,f2]. The one at the head end, the cranial neuropore, closes first, at about day 25 [f1,f2]. The one at the tail end, the caudal neuropore, closes at about day 28 [f2]. Then the tube is sealed and neurulation, the making of the tube, is done [f2]. The closed tube is narrow toward the tail, where it forms the spinal cord [f3]. It is broad toward the head, with swellings, the brain vesicles, that become the brain [f3].
body.mbbs: The cranial (rostral) neuropore closes at about day 25, at the 18–20 somite stage [f1]. The caudal neuropore closes at about day 28, at about 25 somites [f2]. Neurulation is then complete [f2]. These match Carnegie stages 11 and 12 [f1,f2]. The closed tube is narrow caudally, forming the spinal cord [f3]. Cranially it is broad and bears dilatations, the brain vesicles [f3]. Because closure ends by day 28, neural tube defects arise very early [f2,f5].

facts.text: The cranial neuropore, the open head end of the tube, closes at about day 25, at the 18–20 somite stage (Carnegie stage 11).
The caudal neuropore, the open tail end, closes at about day 28, at about 25 somites (Carnegie stage 12); neurulation is then complete.
The closed tube is narrow toward the tail (future spinal cord) and broad toward the head, with swellings, the brain vesicles (future brain).
Beyond Langman: the caudal neuropore's final closure lies at the level of future sacral vertebra 2; the cord below forms by a separate, secondary process.
If the tube fails to close at the head end, the result is anencephaly; failure lower down gives spina bifida, most often lumbosacral.
Taking folic acid around conception prevents a large share of neural tube defects.
Closure ends about day 28 after fertilization (6 weeks after the last period), often before pregnancy is known, so folic acid must start before conception.

misconceptions.wrong: The neural tube closes all at once, or from one end.
misconceptions.right: Closure starts in the neck and zips both ways; the cranial neuropore closes at about day 25, the caudal at about day 28.

misconceptions.wrong: Folic acid works if started once pregnancy is confirmed.
misconceptions.right: The tube closes by about day 28, often before the pregnancy is known, so folic acid must start before conception.

checks.prompt: Put these events in order, earliest first.
options: The raised edges join in the future neck
checks.why: Fusion starts at the neck; then the head-end opening shuts, and the tail-end opening shuts last.

checks.prompt: About when does the caudal neuropore close?
checks.why: The caudal neuropore closes at about day 28; day 25 is the cranial one.

checks.prompt: Why must folic acid start before conception to protect the neural tube?
options: It takes months to reach the embryo
The tube seals in the first month, often before pregnancy is known
It only works on the egg
It is harmful later in pregnancy
checks.why: Closure ends about 6 weeks after the last period, so waiting for a positive test is often too late.

adult: The narrow part becomes the spinal cord; the broad swellings become the brain [f3].
clinical: When the tube fails to close, the result is a neural tube defect [f5]. Failure at the head end gives anencephaly; lower down it gives spina bifida [f5]. Folic acid taken around conception prevents a large share of these defects [f6]. It must start before conception, because closure ends by about day 28 [f6,f7].

remember.q: When does the cranial neuropore close?
When does the caudal neuropore close?
remember.a: About day 28; then the whole tube is sealed [f2].

remember.q: What do the narrow and broad parts of the closed tube become?
remember.a: Narrow tail part: spinal cord; broad head part with brain vesicles: brain [f3].
